text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today, erasing gains from the past two days and retreating from last week's peak. The decline comes as crude oil prices eased slightly (US crude at $91.48/barrel, down from the $136+ levels that boosted the stock early in the week), even as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and Eastern Europe remain acute. A major Trump administration deal to increase Venezuelan oil production could add supply to the market over time, which may be weighing on near-term prices and investor sentiment toward U.S. oil majors.

The longer backdrop matters here: while refinery disruptions from wars in Ukraine and Iran are pushing diesel to record highs, increased Venezuelan supply—combined with the potential for more crude flowing to global markets—creates conflicting pressures on oil majors' stock prices. ConocoPhillips benefits from higher crude prices, but sustained supply growth could moderate the upside.
